markscheme.html:
Correct answer: B

A: Incorrect. A pipe closed at one end supports only odd harmonics (only odd multiples of the fundamental frequency).

B: Correct. A pipe closed at one end has a displacement node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end, so only odd harmonics (odd multiples of the fundamental frequency) are present.

C: Incorrect. All harmonics occur in an open-open pipe or a string fixed at both ends; a closed-open pipe restricts to odd harmonics.

D: Incorrect. Higher resonant modes exist, but they are the odd harmonics (3rd, 5th, …), not just the fundamental.

question.html:
In a pipe closed at one end, what type of harmonics are possible?

  1. Only even harmonics
  2. Only odd harmonics
  3. All harmonics
  4. Only the fundamental
